import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load datasets
crime_df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adjacency_df = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Calculate change in crime rates
crime_df['crime_change'] = crime_df['first_half_2020_value'] - crime_df['second_half_2019_value']

# Standardize the change values
mean_change = crime_df['crime_change'].mean()
std_change = crime_df['crime_change'].std()
crime_df['z_change'] = (crime_df['crime_change'] - mean_change) / std_change

# Create adjacency matrix
boroughs = crime_df['borough'].unique()
n = len(boroughs)
adj_matrix = np.zeros((n, n))

# Map borough names to indices
borough_to_idx = {borough: idx for idx, borough in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Fill adjacency matrix

    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    adj_matrix[i, j] = 1
    adj_matrix[j, i] = 1  # Symmetric relationship

# Row-standardize the adjacency matrix
row_sums = adj_matrix.sum(axis=1)
row_sums[row_sums == 0] = 1  # Avoid division by zero
w_matrix = adj_matrix / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

# Calculate Moran's I
z = crime_df['z_change'].values
n = len(z)
S0 = w_matrix.sum()
z_mean = z.mean()

denominator = np.sum((z - z_mean)**2)
